title: POC scoping - Acme Healthcare - Quality eval plan
summary: POC scoping focused on defining quality evaluation plan for Acme Healthcare's clinical note summarization use case: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination and format checks, scoring methodology, workload sizing and benchmarks. Agreed on 4-week POC with targeted datasets and evaluation metrics. Action items assigned for dataset share, benchmark plan, and loading test schedule.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Start time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Dr. Emily Carter (Acme Head of ML), Raj Patel (PM), Sofia Gomez (Security), Tom Wu (SRE)

Auto sections (note: may be imperfect):
Topics: POC goals, success criteria, dataset sizing, golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination thresholds, scoring approach, timeline
Action items: see bottom

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, and we have Priya from our solutions engineering team; how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Dr. Emily Carter: Good, thanks. We want to nail down how you'll validate quality for the clinical summary model — accuracy and hallucinations are our big concerns.
[00:18] Priya Natarajan: Totally, that is the focus. Today we wanna align on the evaluation plan: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks, how we score, and what benchmarks we'll run. Also confirm dataset sizing and timeline for the POC.
[00:30] Raj Patel: Quick context: our current pipeline generates discharge summaries from EHR notes. We process roughly 1.2M notes a year, peak concurrency around 40 qps but typical is 6-8 qps, average request length ~700 tokens and output ~220 tokens. Latency target for user-facing summaries is P95 < 400ms.
[00:47] Priya: That's really helpful — we'll size the POC sims to mirror your distribution: sequence length histogram, token counts, concurrency. For the quality eval plan we propose three main buckets: 1) golden prompt set for deterministic checks, 2) regression suite with historical examples, 3) hallucination/medical-safety checks plus format validation.
[01:05] Dr. Emily Carter: For golden prompts, we want canonical clinician phrasing and edge cases — diagnoses with rare comorbidities, abbreviated notes, and multi-patient mentions.
[01:15] Jordan: Agreed. We'll ask you to share ~150 golden prompts that cover common + edge conditions; we'll include expected references and a short canonical summary for each as gold label. The golden set is used for exact/near-exact match and format checks.
[01:28] Sofia Gomez: On the security side, we'll need to confirm data handling — redaction of PHI for dataset share, SSO, SOC2 docs. But for the eval plan, we need synthetic or de-identified examples.
[01:38] Priya: Yes, please share de-identified samples or synthetic copies. We'll provide a secure upload link (S3 presigned or transfer) and we can agree on retention windows.
[01:46] Tom Wu: For performance tests, we'll need to know your expected burst behavior — you said 40 qps peak. We'll want to run a load test at 1.5x that to validate headroom.
[01:56] Priya: We'll include a throughput benchmark: target steady-state throughput to match 40 qps and a burst test to 60 qps to validate autoscaling and tail latency. We'll run latency benchmarks at your typical token distribution.
[02:10] Raj: Great. Now scoring: what metrics are you proposing? We need something interpretable for clinicians.
[02:17] Priya: Proposed scoring approach (high level): weighted scoring across Accuracy (factual overlap vs gold), Safety/Hallucination penalty, Format correctness, and Readability. Accuracy will be measured with a mix of automated measures (ROUGE-L, BERTScore) and human adjudication on a sample. Hallucination detection will be partly automated (entity hallucination checks, hallucination classifier) plus human review for high-risk items. Format correctness is strict pass/fail — required fields present, correct date formatting, no PHI leaks.
[02:40] Dr. Emily Carter: Human review is expensive — what's the sample size for adjudication?
[02:44] Priya: For POC, we recommend human review on a stratified sample of 300 examples (random + edge cases from golden/regression sets). Automated metrics across full set (10k-20k samples) to give statistical power.
[02:58] Jordan: Scoring rubric suggestion: Accuracy 50%, Safety/Hallucination 25%, Format 15%, Readability 10%. We can make those weights configurable. Threshold for POC success we suggest: composite score >= 0.78 and hallucination rate < 2% on clinician adjudicated sample. Open to adjustments.
[03:20] Raj: That seems reasonable, but can we set specific pass/fail gates for critical items — e.g., hallucination causing incorrect medication or dosage must be zero on the adjudicated sample?
[03:29] Priya: Yes — we can set hard gates for critical categories. For example, any generated medication/dosage error -> fail. We'll flag as safety-critical and require root-cause.
[03:38] Tom Wu: For bench runs, do you support dedicated infra? We'll likely want dedicated to get stable latency and consistent KV cache behavior.
[03:45] Jordan: For the POC we can do both: hosted to validate quality and dedicated for performance isolation. For accurate latency and throughput numbers we recommend dedicated instances for the load test stage. We'll propose a dedicated config in our POC plan.
[03:56] Dr. Emily Carter: Regression tests — we want to ensure no regressions over time for model updates. How will you set that up?
[04:03] Priya: We'll create a regression suite of ~1,000 historical examples spanning common and problem cases. Each run will compare new model outputs against the last known-good baseline using the same scoring rubric. We'll report deltas and flag any parameterized regressions above thresholds.
[04:17] Dr. Emily Carter: How about hallucination detection specifics?
[04:20] Priya: We'll run two automated checks: 1) entity-level hallucination detector — extract named entities from the generated summary, compare to entities in the source note using fuzzy matching and a whitelist; 2) contradiction detection using an entailment model to ensure summary claims are entailed by source. Items failing automated checks go to human adjudication. We'll provide confusion matrices and examples.
[04:40] Raj: Format checks — our product requires fields: patient name (redacted), diagnosis section, treatment plan, follow-up. We need strict JSON schema validation and a secondary check for date format ISO-8601.
[04:52] Priya: We'll implement JSON schema validators as part of the evaluation pipeline; format failures are immediate fails for format metric. We'll also run token-level cost measurement per output and average latency per token.
[05:02] Jordan: Timeline proposal: Week 0 (kickoff): dataset share and access setup. Week 1: golden prompt and regression suite finalize + synthetic de-id samples. Week 2: initial model runs + automated metric sweep. Week 3: human adjudication sample review + performance load tests (dedicated infra). Week 4: final report and recommendations. So roughly 4 weeks end-to-end for the POC.
[05:23] Dr. Emily Carter: Can we accelerate human review if needed? We can allocate clinicians for two days to do adjudication faster.
[05:30] Priya: That would help — we can compress Week 3 if you can provide adjudicators for a 48-72 hour window.
[05:36] Raj: Deliverables — what will we get at the end?
[05:39] Jordan: Final deliverables: evaluation report (metrics, pass/fail by threshold), regression dashboard, a spreadsheet with all golden prompts and results, examples of hallucinations with root-cause analysis, recommended model config and quantization suggestions to balance cost/latency. We'll also share the benchmark scripts and a playback of the load test.
[05:55] Sofia Gomez: Security docs and controls required before any dataset upload: SOC2 report, encryption at rest, KMS details, retention policy, and an NDA addendum for PHI.
[06:05] Jordan: We'll share SOC2 and a data handling spec. We'll provide SSO/SAML guidance for access and can sign the addendum.
[06:12] Tom Wu: Small note on observability: we want per-request tokens, latency, model version metadata in traces so we can trace regressions back.
[06:20] Priya: We'll expose per-request headers and an identifier; we'll also include model version tags in logs and in the evaluation artifacts.
[06:27] Dr. Emily Carter: Any concerns about cost? We need to know expected cost for the POC, both hosted runs and dedicated runtimes.
[06:33] Jordan: We'll provide a cost estimate: hosted evals cost (per-token) and dedicated node rental estimate for the week of load testing. We'll include cost tradeoffs in the final doc.
[06:41] Raj: Ok let's recap next steps.
[06:44] Jordan: Recap: 1) Acme to share de-identified dataset sample (5k examples) + 150 golden prompts and 1k regression examples by 2026-05-18. 2) Redwood to provide secure upload link, SOC2 docs, and POC plan with dedicated config by 2026-05-17. 3) Schedule load test window in week 3 — propose 2026-06-01 to 06-03. 4) Human adjudication schedule — Acme to confirm clinicians availability.
[07:10] Dr. Emily Carter: Sounds good. Any other questions?
[07:13] Sofia Gomez: Need contact for legal/data addendum.
[07:15] Jordan: I'll loop in our legal contact, and Priya will own the evaluation pipeline.
[07:20] Priya: I'll send the detailed scoring rubric and the evaluation script repo link (private).
[07:24] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the POC kickoff doc and timelines.

End of transcript
